cards.prose: In Matthew the man is healed and then told to *shew thyself to the priest*. Here ten men hear nearly the same word, *Go shew yourselves unto the priests*, and are cleansed *as they went*. Yahusha (Jesus) heals them, and then he sends them down the road Moses laid out.
cards.member_sentence: Ten lepers are sent to the priests as Moses laid down and are cleansed on the way, the same road the healed man in Matthew takes.

cards.prose: He said he had not come to destroy the law or the prophets, and here is the first healing after the Sermon. He touches the leper, and then sends him to the priest with *the gift that Moses commanded*. The word on the mountain and the word to the leper are one word.
cards.member_sentence: He says plainly that he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets, which the sending of the leper to the priest bears out.

cards.prose: Here he sends a healed man to the priest with the gift Moses commanded, and there he walks into *their synagogue* on the Sabbath, where men are waiting to accuse him. His answer, *it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days* (Matthew 12:12), is the same Torah kept in both places, against what had been laid over it.
cards.member_sentence: He enters the synagogue where the man with the withered hand is waiting, and what follows is the Torah kept against the rules laid over it.
cards.flag: The target verse is only the setting; the point lives in the verses after it (the withered hand and the Sabbath answer), so the pair is thin on its own.

cards.prose: In Matthew the gift is the one *Moses commanded*, and he sends the man to give it. In Mark the elders hold up another gift, Corban, as a reason for a man to do nothing for his father or mother. He stands with what Moses said and sets their tradition aside.
cards.member_sentence: Moses said to honour father and mother, and Yahusha (Jesus) holds to that commandment against the tradition that emptied it.

cards.prose: He told the cleansed man to go to the priest *for a testimony unto them*. Some time later, in Jerusalem, *a great company of the priests* are obedient. The testimony that began with a leper carrying his offering to the priest did reach the priesthood.
cards.member_sentence: A great company of the priests become obedient in Jerusalem, so the testimony the cleansed were sent to give the priesthood was heard.

cards.prose: Great crowds follow him down from the mountain, and the first to meet him is a man the Torah required to cry *Unclean, unclean*. The Torah shut him outside, and Yahusha (Jesus) puts out his hand and touches him, then sends him back in through the same Torah, to the priest.
cards.member_sentence: This shows the place the Torah gave the leper, outside and crying unclean, which the touch of Yahusha (Jesus) lifts.

cards.prose: Luke puts him on the road *through the midst of Samaria and Galilee*, and the ten lepers who meet him there get the same word as the man in Matthew: *Go shew yourselves unto the priests* (Luke 17:14). Wherever the road runs, the way back for a leper runs through the priest.
cards.member_sentence: Luke sets the road through Samaria and Galilee where ten lepers meet him and are sent to the priests, the same procedure as in Matthew.
cards.flag: The target verse is only the travel note; the leper scene is in the verses right after it, so I quoted Luke 17:14 to carry the point.

cards.prose: Luke opens the same scene in Capernaum, and what he adds is that the centurion did not come first himself. He sent the elders of the Yahudim (Jews) to speak for him, so the man who comes *beseeching him* in Matthew has already been vouched for.
cards.member_sentence: Luke brings him into Capernaum and tells that the centurion first sent elders of the Yahudim (Jews) to ask on his behalf.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) names the direction, *from the east and west*, and Jeremiah names the same gathering, *from the north country* and *from the coasts of the earth*. The great company that returns is Yashar'el (Israel) coming home to a Father who says *for I am a father to Yashar'el (Israel), and Ephraim is my firstborn* (Jeremiah 31:9).
cards.member_phrase: I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the coasts of the earth
cards.member_sentence: The great company brought back from the north country and the coasts of the earth is the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel) coming home.

cards.prose: The many who come *from the east and west* to sit with the fathers are the ones Paul has in view when he says blindness in part has come on Yashar'el (Israel) *until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in*. They are the scattered seed, long living as Gentiles among the nations, gathered home from every quarter.
cards.member_phrase: that blindness in part is happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in
cards.member_sentence: The fulness of the Gentiles coming in is the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) gathered home, the many who sit down with the fathers.

cards.prose: The sick and the oppressed are brought, and he heals them all. Isaiah said Elohim (God) *will come and save you* (Isaiah 35:4), and that then *the eyes of the blind shall be opened*. Matthew sets this beside the other word, that he *took our infirmities*, and says both are being fulfilled.
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's picture of the day Elohim (God) comes to save, with the eyes of the blind opened, is what these healings show.

cards.prose: Matthew says the healings fulfil what Isaiah spoke. When John sends from prison to ask whether he is the one, Yahusha (Jesus) does not argue, he sends back *those things which ye do hear and see*. The evening at Peter's house is part of that answer.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) answers John in prison by pointing to the same healings Matthew has just shown, as his own credential.

cards.prose: The foxes have holes and the birds have nests, but the Son of Adam has nowhere to lie down. David asked what the *son of Adam* is, *that thou visitest him*, and here the visit has come, to a man with no bed in the land he came to.
cards.member_sentence: David asks what the son of Adam is that Elohim (God) should visit him, and in Matthew the visit has come.

cards.prose: Luke carries the line back until it ends at *the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God)*. When Yahusha (Jesus) calls himself the Son of Adam beside the foxes' holes, he is naming that line, the seed of Adam, and he stands in it with nowhere to lay his head.
cards.member_phrase: which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: Luke's genealogy runs back to Adam, the son of Elohim (God), the lineage the title Son of Adam carries.

cards.prose: The man asks to bury his father, and burying a father is honouring him. Moses wrote *Honour thy father and thy mother* with a promise of long days on the land Yahuah (the LORD) gives, and Yahusha (Jesus) never sets that commandment aside. Whatever his answer means, the fifth commandment stands where it was set.
cards.member_sentence: The fifth commandment is the Torah ground under the disciple's request, and the answer he is given does not remove it.
cards.flag: I left the meaning of 'let the dead bury their dead' itself open and only wrote what it cannot mean, since nothing in the sources settles it.

cards.prose: Joseph said to Pharaoh, *let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father*, nearly what this disciple asks when he wants first to go and bury his father. Pharaoh granted it and Joseph went up. The request is the fathers' own, and nothing in it is a sin.
cards.member_sentence: Joseph asks leave to go up and bury his father and is granted it, the pattern of the fathers behind the disciple's request.

cards.prose: In Mark he turns on those who let a man call his goods Corban and so do nothing for father or mother, *Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition* (Mark 7:13). The one who defends the commandment there is the one speaking in Matthew, so his word to this man cannot be a loosing of it.
cards.member_sentence: Moses said to honour father and mother, and Yahusha (Jesus) defends that commandment against the tradition that emptied it.

cards.prose: The psalm asks who is *like unto thee*, and the next line answers: *Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them* (Psalm 89:9). At the boat the winds and the sea are stilled by a word from the man who was asleep, and the disciples see done what the psalm sang of Yahuah (the LORD).
cards.member_sentence: The psalm asks who is like Yahuah (the LORD) and answers that he rules the raging of the sea, which the disciples see at the boat.

cards.prose: This is the psalm for men in ships, who *see the works of Yahuah (LORD), and his wonders in the deep* (Psalm 107:24). The disciples in the boat are those men, with the waves over the sides, and they see the storm stilled by a word.
cards.member_sentence: Men who go down to the sea in ships see the works of Yahuah (the LORD) in the deep, the same sight the disciples have in the storm.

cards.prose: Job is asked who *shut up the sea with doors*, and the answer comes with the sea's own limit: *Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further* (Job 38:11). The voice that set that boundary is the voice heard from the boat, and the winds and the sea obey it.
cards.member_sentence: Job is asked who shut up the sea with doors and said how far it may come, the authority shown in the boat.

cards.prose: Both stories have a ship in a great storm and one man asleep. Jonah is *fast asleep* because he is running from Yahuah (the LORD), and the storm was sent after him. Yahusha (Jesus) sleeps in peace, wakes, and stills the sea with a word.
cards.member_phrase: But Jonah was gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep
cards.member_sentence: Jonah sleeps in a ship in a storm sent after him, while Yahusha (Jesus) sleeps in peace and stills the storm himself.

cards.prose: In the boat a sleeper wakes and the sea goes calm. Later he says what the boat was showing, *a greater than Jonas is here*, to a generation asking for a sign. The disciples had already seen the sign on the water.
cards.member_phrase: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says a greater than Jonas is here, which the stilled sea in the boat had already shown the disciples.

cards.prose: The spirits cry out to *the Son of Elohim (God)* and ask if he has come to torment them. John says that is what the Son was revealed for, and in the country of the Gergesenes the devil's hold on two men is broken in front of the whole city.
cards.member_phrase: This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil
cards.member_sentence: The Son of Elohim (God) was revealed to undo the works of the devil, which the spirits in the tombs seem to know at once.
cards.flag: The target verse as given in the packet reads in modern wording ('Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil') rather than the KJV-based text the old note quotes; the canon text should be checked.

cards.prose: The cry *before the time* asks about a time already set. Peter says Elohim (God) did not spare the angels that sinned but delivered them into chains *to be reserved unto judgment*, and the spirits in the tombs of the Gergesenes are their offspring and know the same day is waiting.
cards.member_phrase: cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) did not spare the angels that sinned but kept them for judgment, the appointed time the spirits fear in Matthew.
cards.flag: The step from the bound angels to the spirits of their offspring rests on the thread's Enoch material, not on this verse alone.

cards.prose: Jude gives the same reservation a name, *the judgment of the great day*, and the chains kept for the angels who left their own habitation. When the spirits ask if he came *to torment us before the time*, it is that day they have in view.
cards.member_phrase: he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day
cards.member_sentence: The angels who left their first estate are reserved for the judgment of the great day, the day the spirits fear in Matthew.

cards.prose: The Torah calls the swine *unclean to you*, and a herd of them feeding near the tombs says how far the people of that coast had drifted from it. The spirits ask for the herd, the unclean going into the unclean, and the whole herd runs down into the sea.
cards.member_sentence: Moses names the swine as unclean, so the herd beside the tombs is a plain sign of defilement and of a place living away from the Torah.

cards.prose: Moses says it a second time, and here adds *nor touch their dead carcase*. A herd of the animal the commandment names, feeding by the tombs and then lying dead in the sea, is the very picture the commandment keeps a man away from.
cards.member_phrase: ye shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their dead carcase
cards.member_sentence: A second witness in the Torah that the swine are unclean, adding that even their dead carcase was not to be touched.

new_threads.title: Let the dead bury their dead, and the fifth commandment
new_threads.summary_md:
*It ain't new.* The man asks for what the fathers did, and the commandment he stands on was written long before him. One of the disciples says:

*And another of his disciples said unto him, Adonai (Lord), suffer me first to go and bury my father.* (Matthew 8:21)

*But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.* (Matthew 8:22)

Read as a word against honouring a father, that answer would put Yahusha (Jesus) at odds with Moses, in the same Matthew where he has just said he did not come to destroy the law. The commandment is plain:

*Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.* (Exodus 20:12)

The fathers did exactly what this disciple asks. Joseph stood before Pharaoh with the same request:

*My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.* (Genesis 50:5)

And when Yahusha (Jesus) is speaking of this very commandment in Mark, he does not loosen it. He defends it against the elders who had found a way around it:

*For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:* (Mark 7:10)

*Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.* (Mark 7:13)

Whatever he means by the dead burying their dead, the man who says it in Matthew is the man who guards the fifth commandment in Mark, so it cannot be a teaching against honouring a father. What the saying does show is the weight of the call. *Follow me* stands first in the sentence, and the cost is the one he has just named to the scribe, a Son of Adam with nowhere to lay his head.
